A few words to know

folded
Bent so that one part covers another.
enrolment
Officially joining a course.
selected
Chosen from a group.
conditional
Only happening if something else happens.
permission
Agreement that something may be done.
original
The first document rather than a copy.

04 · Read & review

The transcript

Submit all six answers to unlock the transcript. You can then listen and read together.

Two days after meeting Emma, Helen Ward called the newsroom. She had spoken to her cousin, who did not want to meet a journalist. However, the cousin had agreed that Helen could show Emma a copy of the old letter, with the name and address covered. Emma asked whether that permission included taking a copy. Helen said it did not. For now, Emma could read it during another private meeting.

They met in the same quiet room. Sarah stayed outside until Helen agreed that she could join them. Helen took a folded sheet from an envelope and placed it on the table. The foundation's name appeared at the top. Below it was a date in September 2011.

Emma read the letter slowly. It said that the student's application had been selected for travel support. But it also said that payment would depend on proof of enrolment and the final travel costs. The letter was not a promise that money had already been sent.

“So your cousin received a grant?” Sarah asked.

“The letter says selected,” Helen answered. “I don't know when money was paid, or whether it was paid at all.”

Emma pointed to a paragraph at the bottom. It explained that unsuccessful applicants could request a review within fourteen days. The same paragraph appeared in the blank model letter Fiona had sent earlier. But Helen's cousin had been selected, according to this copy. The review paragraph did not tell Emma anything about people who were rejected.

“Do you remember when your cousin got this?” Emma asked.

“No. I remember helping with the application. I found the letter years later among our family papers.”

Emma wrote down the printed date, but not a date of delivery. She also noted that she had seen a copy, not the original. She did not take a photograph or record Helen's words.

When the meeting ended, Helen agreed to ask her cousin whether a copy with personal information removed could be shared for checking. She made no promise. Emma thanked her for asking.

Back at her desk, Emma compared what she had read with the newspaper announcement of eight selected students. One letter described one selection; it could not confirm the newspaper's total. Nor could it establish a payment.

She opened her notebook and wrote: Selected — supported by one unverified copy. Paid — unknown.

A small piece of the story had become clearer. The larger question had not.
